heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 handles Polymaker PolyTerra PLA straight out of the box with exceptional surface finish on its stock stainless steel nozzle and open-frame design. Tuned for a 21 mm³/s volumetric flow limit, this setup reaches a reliable maximum print speed of 250 mm/s without compromising layer adhesion.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (clean with Isopropyl Alcohol or warm dish soap, no adhesive required)
slicerTweaks: Cap the Max Volumetric Speed at 21 mm³/s in the Filament Settings to prevent under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Set Hotend Temperature to 210°C (First Layer 215°C) and Bed Temperature to 55°C for optimal matte finish and bed adhesion.
Enable Pressure Advance calibration with an initial manual value around 0.024 s/mm or use Bambu dynamic flow calibration.
Set Seam Alignment to Scarf Joint with a 10mm scarf length and 0.5mm start height to completely hide the Z-seam on matte surfaces.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak interlayer bonding / brittle prints along Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyTerra PLA contains mineral fillers that reduce natural interlayer weld strength if cooled too aggressively or printed too cold at high linear speeds.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase printing temperature from 210°C to 220°C and reduce the maximum part cooling fan from 100% to 70% in OrcaSlicer filament cooling settings.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing and fuzzy retractions on travels
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Direct drive retraction distance too low or nozzle travel unretracted across open perimeters.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Increase retraction length to 0.8 mm at 30 mm/s, check 'Wipe on Loops', and enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' with a max detour factor of 1.5.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer peeling or corner lifting
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PEI plate contaminated with skin oils or print bed temperature set too low.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Wash the Textured PEI Plate thoroughly with warm water and Dawn dish soap, set bed temperature to 60°C for the first layer, and set first layer speed to 35-40 mm/s.

faq.question: Does Polymaker PolyTerra PLA require a hardened steel nozzle on the Bambu Lab A1?
faq.answer: No. Although PolyTerra uses organic and mineral matte additives, it is non-abrasive and fully compatible with the A1's stock stainless steel nozzle.

faq.question: Can I use cardboard PolyTerra spools directly inside the Bambu Lab AMS Lite?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is strongly recommended to print reusable plastic spool edge rings or snap-on adapters to prevent cardboard dust accumulation and ensure smooth rolling on AMS Lite rotary holders.

faq.question: Why does the surface sheen vary between high-speed and low-speed sections?
faq.answer: Matte PLAs appear glossier when printed hotter or slower. In OrcaSlicer, set consistent outer wall speeds (e.g., 150-200 mm/s) to ensure uniform surface texture throughout the model.

faq.question: Do I need to enclose the Bambu Lab A1 to print PolyTerra PLA?
faq.answer: No, an enclosure is not needed and actually discouraged for PLA. PolyTerra prints best in an open-air environment with ample airflow to prevent heat creep in the toolhead.
